title: Suspension bridge collapses under wedding guests in Kuala Krai
detail: More than 50 people fell into the Chatel Damai river when a worn suspension bridge at Lata Rek collapsed as wedding guests crossed; at least five were injured and none killed. PM Anwar ordered immediate replacement.

title: Wooden bridge collapse cuts off 4,500 villagers in Baram
detail: A wooden bridge in Miri division collapsed after nonstop rain, leaving over 4,500 residents of seven villages including Long Silat and Long Bee without a passable route; the Telang Usan penghulu reported no injuries.

title: Rompin village bridge collapses; seven rescued
detail: A bridge linking Kampung Selendang and Kampung Sungai Mok in Rompin collapsed around 8am; police evacuated seven people including a heavily pregnant woman and the district JKR closed the road.

title: Flood evacuees rise in Sabah and Sarawak
detail: Disaster committee figures cited by Malay Mail put evacuees at 859 at 4pm: 619 in Sabah (Beaufort, Kota Kinabalu, Kota Belud), 213 in Miri, Sarawak, and 27 in Segamat, Johor.

title: Sabah and Sarawak floods displace 1,329
detail: NADMA said 1,329 people from 470 families were at 10 relief centres as of 4pm: 1,224 in Sabah's Beaufort and Tenom and 105 in Miri, Sarawak.

title: Severe continuous rain warning for Sarawak, west Sabah
detail: MetMalaysia issued a severe-level continuous heavy rain warning for Sarawak, western Sabah and Labuan until January 11, citing a monsoon surge, with strong wind and rough sea warnings for the South China Sea extended.

title: Sarawak floods worsen; 41 relief centres open
detail: Sarawak's disaster management committee reported 3,890 evacuees at 41 relief centres across seven divisions, with Serian district declared a disaster red zone; Sabah had 367 evacuees from Beaufort.
attribution: Sarawak JPBN figures via Malay Mail

title: Welding blast kills worker at Melaka recycling centre
detail: Melaka fire and rescue said an explosion during welding at a waste recycling centre in Bukit Rambai Industrial Park killed a 44-year-old man and injured a colleague; a hazmat team monitored for toxic gas.
attribution: Fire and rescue department via Malay Mail

title: Fire guts furniture factory in Sea Park, PJ
detail: Selangor fire and rescue deployed 34 personnel as a furniture factory on Jalan 20/1, Sea Park was engulfed, sending thick smoke across the area; no casualties were reported and the cause was under investigation.
attribution: Fire and rescue department via Malay Mail

title: Muda Dam falls to 20%; PBAPP activates contingency plan
detail: PBAPP said the Muda Dam dropped to 20% on February 20 from 84.6% on January 1 due to dry weather and irrigation releases, and activated its Sungai Muda Contingency Plan 2026 drawing on Mengkuang Dam.

title: M6.8 deep quake off Kudat, strongest in 11 years
detail: MetMalaysia said a magnitude 6.8 quake struck about 49km west of Kudat at 12.57am at a depth of 678km, the strongest to hit Malaysia in 11 years; only mild tremors were felt, with no tsunami threat or damage reported.

title: Peat fire at Kuala Tatau needs aerial water bombing
detail: Bomba said a peat fire of about 5 hectares at Kuala Tatau Serupai burned for four days; a Mi-171 helicopter from the Miri air unit made 15 water-bombing runs by March 26.

title: MetMalaysia: heatwave to last until June
detail: MetMalaysia's director-general said temperatures could reach 37-38C in northern states, peaking mid-March to mid-April; Level 1 alerts covered 17 peninsular areas and Level 2 heatwave warnings three areas.

title: Level 2 heatwave in Perlis, Kedah and Hulu Perak
detail: MetMalaysia placed seven areas at Level 2 heatwave (37-40C for three days), including Perlis, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Sik, Baling and Hulu Perak, with 13 more at Level 1 alert.

title: Kelana Jaya LRT slowdown after train fault
detail: Rapid KL said a train was withdrawn and run manually between KL Sentral and Masjid Jamek, slowing services; FMT noted a power outage and a fallen branch on the line earlier that week and that Prasarana had submitted a recovery plan to Cabinet.

title: Two killed in DUKE chain crash
detail: KL traffic police said a broken-down lorry at KM10.4 of the DUKE between Ayer Panas toll and Ampang triggered a chain collision involving three lorries and a pickup, killing two and injuring three.
agency: Kuala Lumpur Police Traffic Investigation Division

title: Festive road deaths up 17% over CNY and Aidilfitri
detail: IGP Khalid Ismail said Ops Selamat 25 and 26 recorded 90 road deaths (vs 77) and 9,934 accidents, with 144,726 summonses issued.

title: MACC freezes 133 accounts worth RM160m in false import declaration probe
detail: MACC's Operation Celio remanded a company owner, searched 14 sites and froze 133 bank accounts holding about RM160 million under the MACC Act and AMLA, alleging a syndicate of importers and forwarders underdeclared goods since 2020, costing about RM1.5 billion in duties.

title: Thousands rally at Dataran Merdeka over anti-graft chief
detail: Thousands gathered in Kuala Lumpur to demand a Royal Commission of Inquiry into allegations against outgoing MACC chief Azam Baki; police deployed riot gear and armoured vehicles and said they would call in organisers over a firecracker incident.
attribution: Police and participants via The Edge (Bloomberg)

title: Widespread CelcomDigi network disruption
detail: Users reported a widespread CelcomDigi outage affecting mobile data, SMS, navigation apps and cashless payments; FMT said the company had not yet commented and some users called on MCMC to investigate.

title: Sarawak's fourth rabies death of 2026
detail: Sarawak health department said a 63-year-old Bintulu man bitten by a puppy in February died of rabies, the state's fourth death this year and 87th of 94 human cases since the 2017 outbreak declaration.

title: Bukit Aman: 2,251 arrested in four anti-scam operations since January
detail: CCID director Rusdi Mohd Isa said Ops Taring (430 arrests, 270 of them foreigners), Ops Belatuk (403, targeting mule accounts in job and e-commerce scams), Ops Frontier (1,372) and Ops Cenderahati (46) led to 2,251 arrests from January to early May.

title: Flash floods across Klang Valley
detail: Thunderstorms flooded Kuchai Link (fully closed), parts of the NPE near Bangsar, Desa Tun Razak and a Petaling Jaya food court where water was about 1.2m deep; Selangor fire and rescue said no evacuation was needed.
attribution: Fire and rescue department via FMT

title: 46 raids bust international scam ring; 187 held, RM57.68m seized
detail: The Inspector-General of Police said raids on 6-7 May across the Klang Valley and beyond arrested 187 suspects, 129 of them Chinese nationals, over fake investment, Japanese-police impersonation and romance scams, seizing properties, cars and luxury goods worth RM57.68 million.

title: Drought in Kedah rice bowl prompts cloud seeding
detail: PM Anwar Ibrahim announced cloud seeding as the Muda Agricultural Development Authority's main reservoir was reported at about 8% capacity, delaying planting in Malaysia's main rice region.
agency: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security / MADA

title: Migrant boat capsizes off Pangkor; bodies recovered
detail: Perak MMEA said a boat believed carrying 37 Indonesians from Kisaran capsized about 8.2nm northwest of Pulau Pangkor; 23 were rescued and four bodies recovered, with 10 still missing.

title: Southwest Monsoon begins, drier conditions to September
detail: MetMalaysia said the Southwest Monsoon would run from May 14 to September with fewer rainy days, early-morning squall lines on the west coast, and a risk of local and transboundary haze from July to September.

title: Pipe burst in Butterworth cuts Penang supply
detail: PBAPP said a 135cm pipeline on Jalan Raja Uda burst, reportedly due to a third-party contractor, disrupting supply across North Seberang Perai and parts of Southwest Penang Island; the same main burst on May 17.

title: 23 road deaths on first day of Aidiladha
detail: PDRM's traffic department (JSPT) recorded 1,225 accidents and 23 deaths nationwide on May 27, up from 15 deaths the day before.
agency: PDRM Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT)

title: Sarawak dams hit drought emergency levels
detail: Sarawak's disaster committee said Batang Ai and Bakun dams were at Drought Emergency Level 1 and Murum at drought-event status, and launched cloud seeding with NADMA; it also flagged Kuala Baram peatland as high fire risk.

title: 38,842 dengue cases in first half; DENV-3 dominant
detail: Figures reported by The Star put dengue cases at 38,842 from Jan 4 to Jun 27, led by Selangor (17,701), Kuala Lumpur (7,191) and Johor (4,591), with DENV-3 now the dominant serotype.

title: MACC freezes 14 accounts, seizes RM1.4m in immigration syndicate probe
detail: MACC Chief Commissioner Abd Halim Aman said 38 people including enforcement officers and civil servants were arrested midweek over a syndicate abusing social visit passes for foreign workers; 14 accounts holding about RM1.1 million were frozen and RM1.4 million in assets seized in Putrajaya, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka.

title: Home Ministry: online scams cost RM5.37b from 2024 to May 2026
detail: A Home Ministry parliamentary reply put online scam losses at RM5.37 billion from 2024 to May 2026, with fake investment schemes (RM2.68 billion), telecom scams (RM1.54 billion) and e-financial crime making up over 90%.

title: Landslide half-blocks Tapah-Cameron Highlands road
detail: Perak fire and rescue said heavy rain triggered a landslide near Batu 25, about 7km from Ringlet, blocking half the road with rocks and trees; it was cleared by 5.10pm with no casualties.
attribution: Fire and rescue department via The Star

title: Sabah CM: no kidnap-for-ransom in ESSZone since 2020
detail: At the ESSZone joint committee meeting co-chaired with Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Sabah Chief Minister Hajiji Noor said there had been no kidnap-for-ransom cases since January 2020 and security was under control; he urged foreign missions to review travel advisories.
attribution: Sabah Chief Minister via The Star

title: 30-hectare peat fire in Betong; Lundu forest fire controlled
detail: Sarawak fire and rescue reported a 30-hectare peatland fire at Jalan Bungin, Betong with no nearby water source, and a nearly 2-hectare fire in Samunsam Forest Reserve, Lundu, controlled with 13 water-bombing flights.

title: Selangor police shut five scam call centres run from homes; 40 held
detail: Selangor police chief Shazeli Kahar said raids from 18 to 25 August in Sungai Buloh, Bukit Rimau, Kajang and Subang Jaya arrested 40 people, 37 of them foreigners, running love scams, foreign-police impersonation and video-subscription scams from residential premises.

title: Hazardous haze in Serian and Samarahan
detail: APIMS readings at 9am showed 17 areas unhealthy to hazardous, led by Serian (API 374) and Samarahan (306); Kuching reached 295 and Kuala Lumpur 153.

title: Four killed in 11-vehicle pile-up on LPT1
detail: Pahang fire and rescue said an express bus hit a tanker at KM110.4 of the East Coast Expressway near Lanchang, triggering an 11-vehicle pile-up that killed four and injured four; the 30 bus passengers were unhurt.
attribution: Fire and rescue department via The Vibes

title: Penang ferry collides with another vessel
detail: A Penang ferry heading to Butterworth collided with another vessel at 8.35pm, toppling motorcycles on board; passengers reported minor injuries and the ferry docked safely.

title: Haze cancels AirBorneo flights at Kuching
detail: Kuching International Airport said two AirBorneo flights (to Mukah and Tanjung Manis) were cancelled due to haze, while runway visibility stayed at 2,000m, above the 800m minimum.

title: NSRC seized RM7.94m in scam proceeds Jan-July, returned RM5.16m
detail: Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the National Scam Response Centre seized RM7.94 million in scam proceeds from January to July 2026 and returned RM5.16 million (65%) to victims; 746 Malaysians had fallen for fraudulent overseas job offers by late August.

title: Main pipe leak cuts water to 34,000 accounts in Kelantan
detail: Air Kelantan said a leak in a 1,100mm pipe at Pulai Chondong disrupted supply to about 34,000 accounts in Machang, southern Kota Bharu and Pasir Puteh; 24 tankers supplied hospitals and schools.

title: 39 areas at unhealthy API as haze spreads
detail: APIMS showed 39 areas with unhealthy API at 4pm, highest at Johan Setia, Selangor (188), with Cheras 177 and Nilai 176; a cloud seeding operation was reported to begin in the Klang Valley.

title: Exceptionally heavy rain floods Ampang area of KL
detail: KL Mayor Fadlun Mak Ujud said Lembah Keramat recorded 155.5mm of rain, about five times the usual, causing flash floods in Ampang, Taman U-Thant and Jalan Ampang.

title: Thunderstorm warning for KL, Labuan and nine states
detail: MetMalaysia warned of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 9pm across Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and districts in Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah.

title: Cloud seeding for low dams in Johor, Melaka, N. Sembilan
detail: NADMA, MetMalaysia and the natural resources ministry began a four-day cloud-seeding operation to raise dam levels and secure water supply, also as a haze mitigation measure.
